content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson focuses on backtracking fundamentals within Recursion and Backtracking. Start with the specific syllabus items rather than memorizing names: State-Space Trees; Choosing, Exploring, and Undoing; Constraint Checking; Pruning Invalid States. Identify the input, the supported operations, and the condition that makes the algorithm correct.

content_blocks.title: How the subtopics connect
content_blocks.text: The PDF lists the following concepts for this lesson: State-Space Trees; Choosing, Exploring, and Undoing; Constraint Checking; Pruning Invalid States. Treat these as connected parts of one problem-solving workflow. Define the state and assumptions, perform the operation, preserve the needed invariant, then inspect the output.

content_blocks.title: Correctness checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Recursion requires a base case and a smaller subproblem; backtracking additionally restores state between branches. Before relying on the result, state your preconditions, identify the invariant or key argument, and test an input that violates a common assumption.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Implement or trace a small example of backtracking fundamentals. First write one normal input and its expected result, then add a boundary case. Explain why the result is correct and analyze time and auxiliary space.

common_mistakes.why: A normal case may hide empty-input, duplicate-value, ordering, disconnected-input or off-by-one errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, boundary and invalid cases and state which inputs the implementation supports.

common_mistakes.problem: Guessing complexity from the code length.
common_mistakes.why: Loops, nested work, recursion, data structure operations and input properties determine the cost.
common_mistakes.fix: Count dominant operations as a function of input size and distinguish auxiliary memory from input storage.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a code snippet as a complete production implementation.
common_mistakes.why: A teaching example often omits input validation, robust tests or special cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the linked exercise and local tests to extend it; record runtime assumptions and limitations.
